messages:
maria: Heads-up — spotted an S3 access log in staging with an object key that looks like it contains a base64 blob. Not sure if it's just debug data. Pasting the line below. @suresh @eng-security please advise.

maria: s3-access-log: 2026-11-02T12:34:56Z bucket=redwood-staging key=logs/2026/11/02/abcd1234.obj size=2048 user=user-123 agent=redwood-app payload="eyJhbGciOi..."

suresh: On it. Can you DM me the full object path? we need to check if payload contains secrets. If it's in staging maybe lower blast radius but still sensitive.

maria: sent DM with s3://redwood-staging/logs/2026/11/02/abcd1234.obj. I redacted a few chars here. Not sure if rotated.

ops-bot: [automated] S3 object abcd1234 has lifecycle=hot; last_modified=2026-11-02T12:34:56Z; access_policy=private.

kevin: Quick question — is the app supposed to be logging tokens? codepath is: /service/worker -> debug log at worker/processor.go:142

anna: That's unintentional. That debug branch logs request.Body for failed parsers. We should not log body if content-type=application/json with Authorization header. I'll open a PR to change that behavior.

maria: For triage: does this meet incident threshold? i.e., PII/API key exposed to staging S3 only. Any customer data? I think no, just internal keys.

suresh: Initial check: payload contains what looks like an API key-like string and a user email pattern. Marking scope as 'staging-only'. No signs of production access. Recommend: 1) rotate any impacted keys, 2) redact logging in code, 3) run search for similar objects, 4) prepare comms if keys belong to customer. @maria can you confirm if any customer identifier present?

maria: I see "user":"alice@example.com" inside decoded blob. That would be a customer email. So we need comms approval before notifying customers.

kevin: OK — escalate to security review and legal. @legal-team please advise on required notice. Also we should prepare internal incident postmortem and external comms template.

simran (eng-security): Assigned. Adding to incident tracker: INC-2026-187. For now classified as Data Exposure (low-medium) because staging only but includes customer email and API key. Recommend rotating keys and purging object. @ops-sre please purge S3 object and add IAM logs for access.

ops-sre: Will purge object within 30 mins and add access logs. Need confirmation to rotate all staging keys or specific ones?

suresh: Rotate any keys that match the prefix found in blob. Ops to provide list; we'll coordinate with platform team.

maria: Purge completed. Confirmed object removed at 2026-11-02T13:02:10Z. Thanks @ops-sre :thumbsup:

ops-sre: Confirmed. Also replicated object snapshot taken and stored in secured access for forensics.

simran (eng-security): Drafting comms. Internal notify to affected teams now. External comms: hold until legal review. I'll ping when approved.

kevin: Also open a PR for the logging fix — assign to anna. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/service/pull/4567

anna: PR opened and linked to incident. Tests added to ensure request body isn't logged when Authorization is present.

maria: Thanks. Next steps checklist: rotate keys, update logging, search for similar objects, legal review for comms, postmortem doc. I'll maintain the checklist in INC-2026-187.

suresh: Great. If anything else appears, tag this thread. Good job triaging quickly. :white_check_mark:
